description: Storm Events Database is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. This database contains storm data and unusual weather phenomenon reports for the United States from 1950 through the end of a recent month or year. Two search fields give users a way to search for storms that may have impacted their location. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – General, High Winds, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Critical Facilities, Economy, Energy and Utilities, People, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
